editorial:
Imagine finding a giant, run-down hotel by the ocean and deciding to just live there with your best friends. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a group of young people who are tired of the real world and decide to squat in this abandoned building. The vibe is all about freedom, loud parties, and trying to figure out who you are when no one is telling you what to do. It feels like a dream at first, with the kids creating their own little paradise where they can love and laugh without any rules. It is a slow burn that captures that specific feeling of being young and feeling like you can change the world.

What really works is how the movie shows the cracks forming in their perfect little world. The acting feels very real, and you can tell the characters actually care about each other even when they fight. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a lot of action, but the emotional payoff is worth it. It is a great pick for anyone who misses the feeling of summer breaks and rebellious youth.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, the dream of the hotel falls apart. The external pressure from the authorities and the internal fighting between the friends become too much to handle. You see the group split apart as they realize they cannot hide from adulthood forever. The final scenes show the hotel being emptied, leaving the characters to face the real world again. It ends on a sad but honest note about how youth and freedom eventually fade away.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about rebellious youth and finding yourself.
